newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's president asks Yilmaz to form new govt.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's president asks Yilmaz to form new govt.

text.p: Turkish secularist Mesut Yilmaz said the president asked him on Friday to form a new government to replace the coalition of outgoing Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
"A while ago, the president gave me the responsibility to form a new government," Yilmaz told a news conference in the presidential palace.

He said he would submit a government list to President Suleyman Demirel by June 30 to end a political crisis which came to a head on Wednesday with the resignation of Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader.
"In nine days, that is the second Monday from now, I will give the government list to the president," Yilmaz said.
Yilmaz's Motherland Party has only 129 deputies in the 550-seat parliament and may struggle to find enough allies from the squabbling secularist factions to win a confidence vote.

Two leftist parties have pledged their support for Yilmaz but a secularist alliance would still need backing from a small right-wing group and around a dozen defections from the rival conservative True Path Party.
Yilmaz said he favoured early elections in the spring of 1998 to clear up political chaos sparked in February by demands from the secularist military for an anti-Islamist crackdown.
"We are in favour of holding general and local elections together next spring," Yilmaz said.
Erbakan had earlier proposed a revamped coalition led by True Path leader Tansu Ciller, his coalition partner during a stormy year in power.
